original_question: Let K ⊂ Cv be a discretely valued subfield whose algebraic closure K̄ is dense in Cv . Let p ≥ 0 be the residue characteristic of Cv , and let f ∈ Cv (z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Suppose that there are no points ζ ∈ P1Berk at which f has local degree divisible by p. Then every wandering domain of f lies in the attracting basin of a Type II Julia periodic point.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 17.8 in Section 17 (“p-adic and Nonarchimedean Dynamics”), introduced immediately after Theorem 17.7 as the sharper no-wild-points version of the wandering-domain problem. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official statement of Conjecture 17.8 almost verbatim: it includes the discretely valued subfield K ⊂ C_v with dense algebraic closure, the residue characteristic p ≥ 0, the rational map f ∈ C_v(z) of degree at least 2, the hypothesis excluding points of P^1_Berk where the local degree is divisible by p, and the conclusion that every wandering domain lies in the attracting basin of a Type II Julia periodic point. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated explicitly: Section 17 fixes C_v to be algebraically closed and complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

P^1_Berk should be identified as the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and Type II points are Berkovich points corresponding to rational closed disks in C_v. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The phrase “there are no points ζ ∈ P^1_Berk at which f has local degree divisible by p” is exactly the paper’s no-wild-points condition, so that equivalence should be made explicit if the question is to be fully stand-alone. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

A wandering domain should be defined as a connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f that is not preperiodic. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

A Type II Julia periodic point should be unpacked as a periodic Type II point lying in the Berkovich Julia set J_f; the nearby discussion defines both periodic Type II points and the Fatou/Julia sets. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

Your draft is phrased like a theorem, but in the paper this is posed as a conjecture/open problem, not as a proved result. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

For maximum paper-faithfulness, the question should reflect the paper’s motivation: Theorem 17.7 proves the same conclusion under stronger residue-characteristic hypotheses, and the paper says those hypotheses are used mainly to exclude wild behavior before stating Conjecture 17.8. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question: Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value, let P^1_Berk denote the Berkovich projective line over C_v, and let K ⊂ C_v be a discretely valued subfield whose algebraic closure K̄ is dense in C_v. Let p ≥ 0 be the residue characteristic of C_v, and let f ∈ C_v(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Assume that f has no wild points on P^1_Berk, i.e. for every ζ ∈ P^1_Berk the local degree of f at ζ is not divisible by p. Is it true that every wandering domain of f — meaning every connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f that is not preperiodic — lies in the attracting basin of a periodic Type II point contained in the Berkovich Julia set J_f? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the setting above: if f has no wild points in P^1_Berk, must every wandering domain of f lie in the attracting basin of a Type II Julia periodic point? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: This draft is not targeting the broader no-wandering-domains Conjecture 17.6, and it is not merely Theorem 17.7. Rather, it matches the narrower follow-up Conjecture 17.8: after proving in Theorem 17.7 that every wandering domain lies in the attracting basin of a Type II Julia periodic point under stronger hypotheses, the paper states that those hypotheses are used mainly to eliminate wild behavior and then formulates Conjecture 17.8 by replacing them with the explicit condition that no point of P^1_Berk has local degree divisible by p. The surrounding Section 17 discussion supplies exactly the hidden notation your draft leaves implicit: the ambient field C_v, the Berkovich line P^1_Berk, the definition of wild points, the Fatou and Julia sets, periodic Type II points, and wandering domains. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
